title: Testing new clinical-diagnostic Interviews for the assessment of ICD-11 mental disorders in German-Speaking Adults
summary:
Background: Nearly half of the population is affected by a mental disorder—such as an anxiety disorder, a depressive disorder, or a substance use disorder—at some point in their lives. Currently, the presence of a mental disorder can only be reliably determined through interviews. 
Aim: The aim of our research project is to test the feasibility, reliability, and validity of new diagnostic interviews for assessing mental disorders according to the latest ICD-11 criteria in German. ICD stands for “International Classification of Diseases” and is a globally recognized system for the standardized coding of medical diagnoses; 11 refers to the version number, as updates are made at longer intervals based on new scientific findings. Staff at the World Health Organization (WHO) developed two interviews for assessing mental disorders according to ICD-11, which have now been translated into various languages. The Flexible Interview (known as FLII-11) is a so-called standardized interview in which all questions are predetermined, and the interviewer directly codes the respondent’s answers. The Structured Interview (known as SCII-11) is a so-called structured interview in which, in addition to predetermined questions, the interviewer has greater freedom to ask follow-up questions and to evaluate—and thus code—the responses.
Methods: We will interview the participants using the German version of one or both of these interviews on no more than two occasions. In addition, participants will be asked to complete several questionnaires regarding their current mental well-being.
conditions: Mental Disorders (Depressive Disorders, Bipolar Disorders, Anxiety Disorders, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, Hypochondriasis, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorders, Eating Disorders, Addicted Behavior Disorders, Substance Use Disorders, Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder)

interventions.name: A total of approximately 450 participants aged 18 and older will undergo diagnostic interviews twice with a maximum interval of 10 days between sessions. In addition they will complete questionnaires.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults aged 18 years or older
Exclusion criteria:
- Insufficient proficiency in German to follow the diagnostic interview (at least level B2)
- Physical, cognitive, or mental condition that precludes an evaluation (acute psychosis, mania, intoxication, suicidal tendencies, sensory/motor deficits, IQ < 70) 
- Insufficient time to participate in two interviews scheduled no more than 10 days apart (each lasting 60–90 minutes, or longer in exceptional cases, depending on the participants’ responses) and to complete several questionnaires (approx. 30 minutes).
